content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text treats Matthew 1:16 as answered rather than counting it as an unanswered witness, which is the situation K-G4 governs.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. Not counting it obeys this rule.","room":"none","why":"Because the judge says Matthew 1:16 was answered and does not count it as an unanswered witness, the rule's requirement not to count answered verses is satisfied."}
